variables.policy_prompt_for_subgoal: Start each episode with A, press the button: the initial scene shows uncovered cubes, no held container, and no completed press in the observed execution. After the observed execution shows the hand descending onto the button and withdrawing, choose B if no container is held and either the goal requests a single pickup or remaining_target_positions is nonempty. Explicit 'pressed down' text is not required; the low hand contacting the button followed by withdrawal also establishes the press. For B in a single-pickup goal, read the requested color from the goal, locate its cube in the pre-covering frames of the current observation, and follow the covering event to its resting container. If descent is sampled only before and after, select the resting container nearest that observed cube position. For B in a multiple-pickup goal, select the resting container covering the first stored position, using the covering event when visible or the nearest resting container to that position otherwise. Point inside that container's current visible body, not at the button, exposed cube, or another distractor; small differences between stored cube centers and container centers are expected. When a successful lift leaves a container held and the updated remaining_target_positions still has entries, choose C to free the hand. After release, if the list remains nonempty, choose B at the container covering its first position; do not press the button again or pick up the replaced container. A held container with an empty updated list means the requested final pickup is complete, so no further action is needed if execution terminates. A successful lift in a single-pickup goal completes the task; do not prescribe an additional put-down. For a multiple-pickup goal in an unanticipated situation where another menu response is nevertheless required, choose C if holding a container; otherwise choose B at the nearest resting container to the first remaining position if available, and A if neither condition applies.

fields.name: remaining_target_positions
fields.description: For a single-pickup goal, write [] at every decision step; no target position needs to be carried. For a multiple-pickup goal, initialize only at the first decision step, when no incoming memory exists: read the requested cube colors in goal order and write their visible initial [y, x] positions as an ordered list. On subsequent decisions, an empty list means no pickups remain and must not be reinitialized. Otherwise carry the incoming list unchanged unless the observed execution shows a previously resting container at the first listed position being grasped and lifted, with that container now held and its cube exposed; then remove that first entry. Require a new resting-to-held transition: a container already held at the beginning of a put-down execution must not trigger another removal. Do not remove an entry merely because a pickup is being selected, and do not restore entries after release. Preserve stored coordinates rather than updating them from shifted visible-pixel centers. e.g. [[92, 93], [128, 118]]
fields.annotation: For goals requesting multiple container pickups, an ordered list of the original cube positions for requested container pickups not yet completed, in goal order. Initialize from the visible cubes at the first decision step, including only requested colors. For a single-pickup goal, write [] at every decision step: recover the target from the pre-covering frames and covering event in the pickup decision's observation instead. Retain the original coordinates despite pixel wobble or subsequent covering. Remove the first entry at the decision step showing that its container has actually been grasped and lifted, not at the step selecting the pickup. Putting a container back does not restore its entry. Thus episode 71 has [[92, 93], [128, 118]] at steps 1 and 2 and [[128, 118]] at steps 3 and 4. Single-pickup episodes instead have [] throughout. e.g. [[92, 93], [128, 118]]

history.critique:
field remaining_target_positions, ANNOTATOR PROMPT
  Delete this field. In the supplied trajectories, the goal requests pressing the button and then lifting the container hiding one named cube. The initial decision shows the colored cubes; the next decision's execution window again shows those cubes before the containers descend, followed by the button press. The annotated memory retained the requested cube's original position, for example [[114, 175]], but that position and its covering container are recoverable from the very observation where the pickup is selected. The field was read at none of the decisions, and no incorrect subgoal was reported. This is a NECESSITY failure, not a SUFFICIENCY or PREDICTABILITY failure. Remove the field and its initialization, retention, and removal annotations rather than replacing it with another field.

field remaining_target_positions, POLICY PROMPT
  Delete this field and all instructions for maintaining it. For the supplied single-pickup tasks, the decision after pressing the button includes an early frame with the requested colored cube still visible and later frames showing the container covering it. Thus the policy can recover the target association locally when needed; carrying an original position such as [[114, 175]] duplicates the current observation and breaks NECESSITY. Do not initialize a target list or maintain pickup-completion updates. No replacement memory field is required for these trajectories.

the policy prompt for subgoal
  The supplied trajectories request one container pickup after a button press. At the pickup decision, the observed execution includes both the colored cubes before covering and the containers afterward. No wrong subgoal was reported, but the existing rules unnecessarily make target selection depend on an unread stored list, a NECESSITY failure. Retain A for the initial scene with uncovered cubes and no completed press in the observed execution. Retain recognition of a completed press from low hand contact with the button followed by withdrawal, without requiring explicit pressed-down text. After that press, with no container held, choose B: read the requested color from the goal, locate that cube in the pre-covering frames of the current observation, and follow the covering event to its resting container. Where the descent is only sampled before and after, select the resting container nearest that observed cube position. Point inside its current visible body. Replace references to the first stored position with this observation-local association. Remove rules for list removal, remaining-list tests, intermediate put-downs, and list-dependent fallback actions: they address multiple-pickup continuation not present in the supplied trajectories. A successful lift of the requested container completes these single-pickup goals; do not prescribe an additional put-down.
